abstract: Whether directed strongly regular graphs with parameters $(30, 12, 11, 4, 5)$ or the complementary $(30, 17, 16, 9, 10)$ exist has been an open question: both sets are open in the table of Hobart and Brouwer. We prove that no such graphs exist. Since $t = k - 1$, the one-way arcs form a permutation $\pi$ of the vertices, and the reciprocal pairs form a symmetric matrix $U$. Two lemmas follow from the defining equation. First, inside a cycle of $\pi$ of length $L \ge 4$, the reciprocal adjacency of vertices $d$ steps apart alternates along the cycle for $2 \le d \le L - 2$. Hence cycle lengths are 3 or multiples of 4, and an edge count rules out a cycle of length 24. Second, in the eigenbasis of $\pi$, the off-diagonal coefficients of $U$ link only frequencies with opposite sines, and the norm of the image of an eigenvector is determined by its frequency. Of the 76 cycle types allowed by the simplest condition, the lemmas leave two: $[3^{10}]$ and $[12, 12, 3, 3]$. For $[3^{10}]$, the block-count matrix of $U$ is unique up to permutation and described through the Petersen graph. The SAT solver CaDiCaL finds both remaining formulas unsatisfiable in seconds; its DRAT proofs are verified by drat-trim, and the LRAT proofs derived from them by an independent checker. Controls include satisfiable formulas on known graphs with $t = k - 1$ and certificates for every type excluded by hand. Limitation: we have no graph with $t = k - 1$ and $\mu - \lambda = 1$ in which $\pi$ has cycles longer than 3, so the formula of type $[12, 12, 3, 3]$ is untested on such a graph.
author: meleta
change_summary: Two clarifications requested in the review of version 1. (1) The abstract and contribution 2 now state Lemma 4 for the off-diagonal coefficients of U in the eigenbasis of π; the diagonal coefficient is generally nonzero, as Lemma 4 itself says. (2) Bit-for-bit reproduction is now claimed for the formulas only. A proof is accepted by verifying it, since another build of CaDiCaL or drat-trim may write other DRAT or LRAT files; Sections 1, 2, 7 and 9 and the supplement README say so, and Section 7 reports the reviewer's rerun. (3) The abstract no longer names the concurrent paper; it is cited and compared in the Concurrent work paragraph and in Section 2. The mathematics, the formulas and the results are unchanged.
title: Directed strongly regular graphs with t = k − 1 and μ − λ = 1: structure lemmas and an independent proof that (30, 12, 11, 4, 5) and (30, 17, 16, 9, 10) do not exist
